about: LBTerm's performance budgets (lbterm/PERF.md, 'The budget runner'). lbterm.ps1 budgets sets each scenario up in a test window (perf/budgets.ps1), measures it -Runs times and holds each metric's median to its max. At rest the defaults are what rest should cost, not what a build measured: nothing paints, and the terminal's processes spend next to nothing. A scenario that repaints at rest on purpose (a blinking cursor) has its own, from what the build measured with headroom. Never raise one to pass a scenario: a failure at rest is a bug to fix (its bug says which).

pc.why: When a span or a run counts as measured on a busy PC, and is taken again (PERF.md, 'The PC while it measured'). A test window runs at below-normal priority on its warden job's CPUs, so whatever else wants them comes first: with others on half of their time, all four are taken at once about one moment in sixteen, and a wake waits. Lachlan's PC runs 8 or more Claude sessions beside the tests, which took 14 to 40% of every CPU on 2026-11-03, so the rules are where the measuring starts to suffer, not where the PC is quiet. A scenario judged on too few calm ones that's over budget is busy, not a failure.

frames.why: at rest nothing paints: one stray frame in a 5 s span at most

requests.why: nothing asks for a frame at rest

timers.why: Lachlan's update-status tick (every 20 s) and little else

tasks.why: the update-status tick's few Lua runs, and the cli listener answering a connection now and then (PERF.md, finding 9)

gui_thread_ms.why: the GUI thread asleep: 0.2% of a core

cpu_ms.why: the GUI process asleep, its other threads included: 0.5% of a core

server_cpu_ms.why: the mux server asleep

conpty_cpu_ms.why: the conpty hosts asleep, with nothing printed

busy.about: A busy scenario paints on purpose: its open tab rewrites a line every 50 ms, as a working Claude Code session's spinner turns, so the window paints a frame for each (20 a second measured) and whatever is open over the panes is drawn again with it. What's held is what a frame costs with it open (frame_ms, against busy-one-tab's and busy-tabs' with nothing open) and that nothing is laid out again while what it shows stays the same (words); these are the budgets every busy scenario has, over the rest's, from the seven scenarios' two rounds on 2026-10-31 (06:09 to 06:18, interleaved with the build before; PERF.md, "What the cards cost"), and each scenario holds its own frame_ms and pass_ms

frames.why: the ticker's frames: a line every 50 ms, 19.9 to 20.5 a second measured

requests.why: a request a frame, the ticker's output asking for it: 19.8 to 20.2 a second measured

timers.why: nothing the ticker does arms a timer: 0 to 0.4 a second measured, as at rest

tasks.why: six task runs a frame (the mux client's poll of the pane and its replies, the frame's own): 119 to 123 a second measured

task_ms.why: what those take, 2.9 to 4.9 ms a second measured (a paint isn't a task's)

gui_thread_ms.why: 1.5 times the busiest scenario's slowest round, 96.1 ms (busy-inbox-list); each scenario's frame_ms holds it closer

cpu_ms.why: 1.5 times the slowest round's, 109.1 ms (busy-inbox-list)

server_cpu_ms.why: the mux server reading the ticker's output and handing the GUI each frame's changes: 1.5 times the slowest round's, 72.1 ms

conpty_cpu_ms.why: the ticker's conpty host, 1.1 to 1.3 ms a second measured

words.why: nothing the cards, lists or the rail show changes while the ticker turns: no word laid out again (lbterm_extras::kept), an age moving on now and then at most

missed.why: every refresh of the window's screen while its motion plays gets a frame: DWM plays it, whatever the GUI thread does (lbterm/COMPOSITOR.md), so one missed is DWM or the GPU falling behind. Judged only where the window could be seen (PERF.md, "What's hard to time")
